summary: Khenpo Dazer worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both Shrisingha Shedra and the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Shechen Monastery under Jamgon Kongtrul II, Shechen Kongtrul, and Karsé Kongtrul, later serving as senior teacher there and as founding dean at Surmang Monastery (~1957–1958).

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Thrangu Monastery and under the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later teaching at Rumtek Monastery and serving as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra.
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen (born 1946) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Bokar Rinpoche, and he also taught Kalu Rinpoche.
Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Kunzang Pelden, Mipam Gyatso, Tubten Chokyi Dorje, and Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Zopa Tarchin, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Lama Zolpa Trinlé, later serving as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery (~1977) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Dudjom Rinpoche, Kangyour Rinpoché, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Jé Kar Lama Gönpo Sam Drub, teaching at Tokyo, Kyoto, and Virginia.

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under numerous masters including Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1959–1968).
Khunu Rinpoche (1894–1977) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das and Dev Narayan Tripathi, and he taught at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa.
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was a Tibetology scholar. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.

Khyentse Norbu (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London, as well as under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Pema Wangchok Gyelpo and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where he was attested in 1983 and attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and was taught in 2013 by Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, John Kieschnick, Barend J. ter Haar, and Seishi Karashima.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo, and University of Freiburg. He served as professor and assistant at Tokyo, held deanships at Hokkaido University, and was a professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kim Gutschow, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (born 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

Kim Plofker (born 1964) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Haverford and Brown under David Pingree, and held posts at Brown, Dibner Institute, Utrecht, MIT, and Union College, where she became associate professor in 2019.
